programme: No single recognizable programme unifies these twelve factors. They are a heterogeneous collection of lineage-specifying developmental transcription factors, each associated with a different, unrelated embryonic programme: PAX4/ARX/ISL1-adjacent pancreatic endocrine specification (PAX4), craniofacial/tooth patterning (PAX9), sympathetic/autonomic neuron differentiation via catecholamine synthesis genes DBH/TH/SLC6A2 (PHOX2B), photoreceptor identity via RHO/CRX/NRL/RCVRN (NR2E3), lung and thyroid epithelial identity via SFTPB/SFTPC/SCGB1A1/TPO (NKX2-1), paraxial mesoderm/somite differentiation (TCF15), muscle satellite cell/myogenic specification (PAX7, overlapping ASCL2 at CKM), intestinal stem cell/Tfh identity (ASCL2), and testis-restricted chromatin insulation (CTCFL). PBRM1 and SMARCA1 both point at SWI/SNF (PBAF/BAF) chromatin remodeling, but that pairing is too generic and too thinly supported by the other ten factors to be called the programme these two diseases share.
role_in_a: not applicable — no shared programme was identified to assign a disease-specific role to
role_in_b: not applicable — no shared programme was identified to assign a disease-specific role to
shared_axis: None identified. The concordant factors specify cell fates (pancreas, craniofacial mesenchyme, autonomic neurons, photoreceptors, lung/thyroid epithelium, somite, muscle, gut) that are not the tissues affected in COVID-19 (blood/lung immune-epithelial interface) or psoriasis (skin), and no immune or interferon/IL-17-pathway factor survived concordance filtering to link them.
reasoning: The factors do not converge on a nameable process: each is best known for specifying a distinct, disease-irrelevant embryonic lineage, and the two factors that do share a functional class (PBRM1, SMARCA1 — SWI/SNF subunits) are only two of twelve and are not independently placed in either disease. The literature record is essentially empty for both diseases (Open Targets has no psoriasis association for any of the twelve factors, and COVID-19 associations are all sub-95th-percentile or absent), and the one retrieved paper touching COVID-19 (PHOX2B, PMID 38043520) mentions the pandemic only in passing, not a PHOX2B mechanism. Forcing a story here would mean building it from tissue overlap in target gene lists (e.g., CALCA, BMP4, TP53) that are generic hub genes rather than evidence of a shared regulatory axis.
support: PMID 38043520 discusses PHOX2B in congenital central hypoventilation syndrome and references the COVID-19 pandemic only in the context of facemask use, not a PHOX2B-COVID-19 mechanism — this is the only retrieved paper that even co-occurs with one of the two diseases. All other retrieved papers are off-topic relative to COVID-19 and psoriasis (PMID 40949898: NF-κB2/immune dysfunction, ASCL2 focus unclear; PMID 33671373: mouse vaccine/colon cancer antigen; PMID 35132075: CTCFL in ovarian cancer; PMID 40755411: PAX4 in pig taste organoids/insulin; PMID 27874104: NR2E3 in retinal dystrophy; PBRM1 papers on mycoplasma pneumonia and renal cell carcinoma; PAX7 papers on muscle, sarcoma, obesity; NKX2-1 papers on lung biology and rare disorders).
how_to_falsify: Test whether PBRM1 and/or SMARCA1 occupy immune-relevant loci (e.g., IL10, CSF2, or interferon-stimulated genes) in COVID-19 PBMCs and psoriatic keratinocytes/skin-infiltrating cells using ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN, and check whether that occupancy is disease-enriched relative to matched healthy tissue. If binding at shared immune loci is found and replicates across independent cohorts, a genuine chromatin-remodeling axis would be supported and this incoherent call would need to be revisited; absence of such binding, or binding confined to the lineage-specific targets already listed (SMARCA4, CREBBP, developmental genes), would confirm that these factors are not operating as a disease-relevant module.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood (COVID-19) vs skin (psoriasis), drawn from 32 patient-group comparisons across 4 independent cohort pairs — a broad base, but the concordant factors it yields are dominated by developmental/lineage TFs rather than known blood- or skin-immune regulators. CTCFL is observed bound at 0 of 7 of its listed targets in ReMap, weakening confidence in that factor's target set specifically. The single-view exclusions (STAT2, BACH2, FOXO3, BCL11B) are notable because they are the more immunologically intuitive candidates (interferon signaling, Treg/Tfh biology) and their exclusion — for recurring in only one patient subgroup — is exactly why no interferon- or IL-17-pathway factor appears in the surviving list. The tissue-generic exclusion list (CEBPB, E2F1/E2F3, BCL6, NFATC2, AR, FOXO1/FOXO3, TAL1, KLF1, PBX1, CEBPD) removed the blood/skin master regulators that might otherwise have anchored a believable immune story, which is consistent with — not contrary to — the conclusion that what remains does not form one.
